original_question: For every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, is the sum of the absolute values of the linear Fourier coefficients bounded by sqrt(deg(f))?
target_in_paper: The unsectioned open problem titled "Linear Coefficients versus Total Degree".
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right open problem, the correct domain and codomain f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1}, the fact that the question concerns the degree-1 Fourier coefficients, and the paper's main sqrt(deg(f)) upper-bound target.
missing_details: The paper's statement is about the signed sum sum_{i=1}^n hat f(i), not the sum of absolute values sum_{i=1}^n |hat f(i)|. Adding absolute values makes the question strictly broader and no longer paper-faithful.
The notation hat f(i) should be defined as the singleton Fourier-Walsh coefficient hat f({i}) in the standard Fourier expansion on the uniform hypercube.
The ambient expansion should be specified: f(x)=sum_{S subseteq [n]} hat f(S) prod_{j in S} x_j.
The meaning of deg(f) should be made explicit: the total degree of the unique multilinear real polynomial representation of f, equivalently max{|S| : hat f(S) != 0}.
The question should quantify over all n and all Boolean functions on {-1,1}^n, not leave n implicit.
To be fully stand-alone, it should say that the Fourier coefficients are taken with respect to the uniform measure on {-1,1}^n.

The nearby paper context notes a stronger candidate upper bound, namely k * binom(k-1,(k-1)/2) * 2^(1-k) with k=deg(f), achieved by Majority on k bits; this is not the official statement, but it clarifies the intended scale of the conjecture.
The nearby paper context also records that the only general bound mentioned there is the trivial inequality sum_{i=1}^n hat f(i) <= I[f] <= deg(f), where I[f] is total influence.
refined_question: Is it true that for every Boolean function f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1}, if f(x)=sum_{S subseteq [n]} hat f(S) prod_{j in S} x_j is its standard Fourier-Walsh (equivalently, unique multilinear real) expansion under the uniform measure, and deg(f)=max{|S|: hat f(S) != 0}, then one has sum_{i=1}^n hat f({i}) <= sqrt(deg(f))?
justification: This draft is clearly aiming at the paper's page-9 problem "Linear Coefficients versus Total Degree." The official statement there is exactly the signed first-level Fourier inequality sum_{i=1}^n hat f(i) <= sqrt(deg(f)); it does not use absolute values. The two remark bullets immediately below it supply the intended context: a stronger candidate bound k * binom(k-1,(k-1)/2) * 2^(1-k), attained by Majority on k bits, and the observation that no bound better than the trivial sum_{i=1}^n hat f(i) <= I[f] <= deg(f) was apparently known at the time. Because your draft changes the signed sum to a sum of absolute values and leaves the Fourier/degree conventions implicit, it needs sharpening to match the paper faithfully.
